newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS DEFY LOGIC AGAIN WITH FREE KICK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS DEFY LOGIC AGAIN WITH FREE KICK.

text.p: Roberto Carlos has not only succeeded Branco as Brazil's left back but also as a free kick expert, putting an astonishing swerve on the ball to score in the world champions' 1-1 draw with France.

When Brazil were awarded the free kick in the opening Tournoi de France match on Tuesday, the Real Madrid player ran at the ball, about 35 metres in front of goal, in a straight line, striking it with the outside of his left foot.
Had the ball also gone straight it would have hit one of France's four-man wall in the midriff or gone ballooning into the stand behind Fabien Barthez's goal.

But it bent round the wall and took a wicked swing inwards close to the goal, going in off the post to the astonishment of the Monaco 'keeper, who was rooted to the spot, and giving Brazil a 1-0 lead after 21 minutes.
"I had already scored a similar goal gainst Roma in the Italian league (playing for Internazionale), but it was during play, not a free kick," Roberto Carlos said.

"Against France it's an important goal for my career. But most important, we all recovered after our defeat in Oslo (4-2 to Norway on Friday). And you'll see, it will all go better and better for Brazil."
Captain Dunga recalled a similar goal from a free kick against Chile during the qualifiers for the 1994 World Cup, but he did not say who scored it.
World Cup left back Branco is renowned for his bullet free kicks, scoring a crucial winner with one against the Netherlands in the 1994 quarter-finals to give Brazil a 3-2 victory.
Barthez blamed himself for conceding the goal.
"I lined up my wall badly. Once the ball is hit it's too late for me. I think that goal was my fault," he said.
"But it's true it was a superb shot. It was too fast, I thought it was going out. Fortunately, I haven't often let in goals like that. Otherwise, I felt very good."
Brazil coach Mario Zagallo did not disagree, saying that Barthez had stood between his team and a victory.
"I think that but for the French goalkeeper we could have won this match 3-1," he said.
Barthez tipped stinging shots from Ronaldo and Cafu over the bar in the first half and also had to dive to his left to save a drive from outside the box by Dunga in the second.
France, who had less clear-cut chances, equalised through Karlsruhe striker Marc Keller with his first international goal in the 60th minute.

The French had the better of the second half, according to central defender Marcel Desailly after a roasting from coach Aime Jacquet during haftime in which he accused his players of being afraid of the Brazilians.

Young attacking midfielder Ibrahim Ba, who will be joining Desailly at AC Milan for the new season, said after helping lay on France's equaliser: "We spent too much time watching Brazil play. Afterwards, we showed something else."
